This file provides structural interpretation only. It does not assign routing authority, readiness tiers, Atlas topology authority, jurisdiction rankings, or deployment suitability.

## Institutional Continuity Environment

For builder interpretation, India reads as an institutional continuity environment supported by Aadhaar systems, DigiLocker systems, UMANG systems, India Stack systems, RBI systems, NPCI systems, NIC systems, MeghRaj systems, NKN systems, NIXI systems, CERT-In systems, NCIIPC systems, BharatNet systems, and India Stack Global interoperability structures. These conditions support a builder-facing reading centered on institutional continuity carried through interoperable identity systems, public digital-service infrastructure, central-bank-operated settlement systems, public-sector cloud environments, registry-governance systems, research-network federation, broadband-expansion systems, and cybersecurity coordination structures operating at population scale rather than centralized sovereign-command authority.

## Digital Governance and Identity Environment

For builder interpretation, India reads as a digital-governance interoperability environment supported by Aadhaar systems, DigiLocker systems, UMANG systems, India Stack systems, Digital India systems, and public-service interoperability environments. These conditions support a builder-facing reading centered on digital-governance continuity carried through interoperable identity systems, digital-document infrastructure, unified public-service aggregation systems, and nationally coordinated procedural digitization environments operating at population scale.

## Financial Infrastructure and Settlement Environment

For builder interpretation, India reads as a payment modernization and settlement-governance environment supported by RBI RTGS systems, NEFT systems, NPCI systems, UPI infrastructure, instant-payment interoperability systems, and cross-border payment linkage environments. These conditions support a builder-facing reading centered on payment-system continuity carried through central-bank-operated settlement infrastructure, nationwide electronic-transfer systems, instant-payment interoperability environments, and cross-border digital-payment interfaces rather than globally dominant settlement authority.

## Data Infrastructure and Digital Continuity Environment

For builder interpretation, India reads as a public-sector digital continuity environment supported by NIC infrastructure systems, National Data Centres, MeghRaj cloud systems, hosted governance platforms, and mixed-provider infrastructure systems. These conditions support a builder-facing reading centered on public-sector digital continuity carried through nationally coordinated ICT infrastructure, distributed government data-centre environments, public cloud-service frameworks, and hosted governance platforms rather than a wholly sovereign hyperscale stack.

## Research Network and Scientific Compute Environment

For builder interpretation, India reads as a scientific-network and research-compute federation environment supported by NKN systems, National Supercomputing Mission systems, distributed supercomputing infrastructure, and scientific-network federation systems. These conditions support a builder-facing reading centered on scientific-network federation continuity carried through nationally coordinated research-network infrastructure and distributed supercomputing systems integrated through shared academic-network environments.

## Internet Exchange and Registry Governance Environment

For builder interpretation, India reads as an internet-governance and exchange environment supported by NIXI systems, .IN Registry governance systems, IRINN numbering systems, and domestic peering coordination environments. These conditions support a builder-facing reading centered on registry and exchange continuity carried through nationally administered domain-governance systems, domestic peering coordination environments, and numbering-resource administration systems.

## Telecommunications and Connectivity Environment

For builder interpretation, India reads as a telecommunications and connectivity environment supported by BharatNet systems, NOFN systems, POWERGRID telecom infrastructure, rural broadband-expansion environments, and institutional networking systems. These conditions support a builder-facing reading centered on telecommunications continuity carried through nationwide broadband-expansion systems, institutional networking environments, and state-linked fiber infrastructure.

## Energy and Grid Coordination Environment

For builder interpretation, India reads as an energy-grid operational-coordination environment supported by NLDC systems, GRID-INDIA coordination systems, national-grid synchronization environments, and cross-border power-coordination systems. These conditions support a builder-facing reading centered on energy-grid continuity carried through nationally coordinated load-dispatch systems and synchronized national-grid management environments.

## Logistics and Trade Connectivity Environment

For builder interpretation, India reads as a logistics and trade-connectivity environment supported by major-port throughput infrastructure, JNPA logistics systems, port-expansion environments, and maritime trade-connectivity infrastructure. These conditions support a builder-facing reading centered on global logistics continuity carried through high-throughput maritime infrastructure, port-expansion systems, and maritime trade-connectivity environments.

## Cybersecurity and Critical Infrastructure Environment

For builder interpretation, India reads as a cybersecurity and critical-infrastructure coordination environment supported by CERT-In systems, NCIIPC systems, incident-response coordination infrastructure, and critical-infrastructure protection systems. These conditions support a builder-facing reading centered on cybersecurity continuity carried through national incident-response coordination systems, critical-infrastructure protection environments, and vulnerability-coordination mechanisms.

## Global Digital Public Infrastructure and Cross-Border Integration Environment

For builder interpretation, India reads as a global digital-public-infrastructure and cross-border interoperability environment supported by India Stack Global systems, UPI-PayNow linkage systems, cross-border remittance systems, and international interoperability environments. These conditions support a builder-facing reading centered on cross-border institutional integration continuity carried through digital-public-infrastructure export frameworks, international payment-linkage systems, and outward-facing interoperability initiatives.

## Builder Mode Summary Statement

India appears in builder mode as a large-scale digital-public-infrastructure jurisdiction combining interoperable identity systems, central-bank-operated settlement infrastructure, instant-payment modernization, public-sector cloud continuity, research-network federation, broadband expansion, registry governance, cybersecurity coordination, and globally connected digital-public-infrastructure interfaces.

# India — Profile

Profile derivation constraint: profile content derives strictly from evidence.md, signals.md, trust-dimensions.md, and metadata.md.

## Jurisdiction Overview

India is characterized as a New Delhi-centered large-scale South Asian digital-public-infrastructure environment, an Aadhaar-, DigiLocker-, UMANG-, and India Stack-linked digital-governance and interoperability environment, an RBI-, NPCI-, RTGS-, NEFT-, and UPI-linked payment modernization and settlement-governance environment, a NIC-, MeghRaj-, and National Data Centre-linked public-sector cloud and procedural-digitization environment, a NIXI-, .IN Registry-, and IRINN-linked registry and numbering-governance environment, an NKN- and National Supercomputing Mission-linked research-network and distributed-compute federation environment, a BharatNet-, POWERGRID telecom-, and institutional-network-linked telecommunications and broadband-expansion environment, an NLDC- and GRID-INDIA-linked energy-grid operational-coordination environment, a JNPA-, major-port-, and maritime trade-connectivity-linked logistics environment, a CERT-In- and NCIIPC-linked cybersecurity and critical-infrastructure coordination environment, and an India Stack Global- and globally integrated interoperability environment.

## Digital Governance and Identity Environment

India's digital governance and identity environment is characterized by Aadhaar systems, DigiLocker systems, UMANG systems, India Stack systems, Digital India systems, and public-service interoperability systems. Aadhaar carries continuity through a verifiable population-scale identity environment. DigiLocker provides the secure document-storage, sharing, and verification environment. UMANG is the unified public-service aggregation surface across central and state systems. India Stack and Digital India provide the coordinated interoperability framing linking identity, document, payment, and procedural-service systems.

## Financial Infrastructure and Settlement Environment

India's financial infrastructure and settlement environment is characterized by RBI RTGS systems, NEFT systems, NPCI systems, UPI infrastructure, instant-payment interoperability systems, and cross-border payment linkage environments. RBI carries payment continuity through central-bank-operated settlement infrastructure. RTGS and NEFT are the standing large-value and nationwide electronic-transfer foundations. NPCI and UPI preserve the interoperable instant-payment layer. The UPI-PayNow linkage preserves a documented cross-border payment interface.

## Data Infrastructure and Digital Continuity Environment

India's data infrastructure and digital continuity environment is characterized by NIC infrastructure systems, National Data Centres, MeghRaj cloud systems, hosted governance platforms, and mixed-provider infrastructure systems. NIC carries continuity through nationally coordinated ICT infrastructure spanning NICNET, NKN, National Data Centres, and National Cloud services. The current package preserves a mixed-provider infrastructure boundary rather than a wholly sovereign hyperscale stack.

## Research Network and Scientific Compute Environment

India's research network and scientific compute environment is characterized by NKN systems, National Supercomputing Mission systems, distributed supercomputing infrastructure, and scientific-network federation systems. NKN carries continuity through a nationally coordinated research-network environment. The National Supercomputing Mission preserves the distributed supercomputing framework attached to NKN-linked integration across multiple sites.

## Internet Exchange and Registry Governance Environment

India's internet exchange and registry governance environment is characterized by NIXI systems, .IN Registry governance systems, IRINN numbering systems, and domestic peering coordination environments. NIXI carries continuity through a nationally administered domestic peering environment. The .IN Registry preserves the formal domain-governance environment under NIXI authority. IRINN preserves the numbering-resource administration environment for IP addresses and AS numbers.

## Telecommunications and Connectivity Environment

India's telecommunications and connectivity environment is characterized by BharatNet systems, NOFN systems, POWERGRID telecom infrastructure, rural broadband-expansion environments, and institutional networking systems. BharatNet and NOFN carry continuity through a nationally coordinated middle-mile and rural broadband-expansion environment.

## Energy and Grid Coordination Environment

India's energy and grid coordination environment is characterized by NLDC systems, GRID-INDIA coordination systems, national-grid synchronization environments, and cross-border power-coordination systems. NLDC carries continuity through nationally coordinated load-dispatch functions. GRID-INDIA preserves the synchronized national-grid coordination surface linking restoration, operational coordination, and planning feedback across the national power system.

## Logistics and Trade Connectivity Environment

India's logistics and trade connectivity environment is characterized by major-port throughput infrastructure, JNPA logistics systems, port-expansion environments, and maritime trade-connectivity infrastructure. Major-port throughput carries continuity through high-volume maritime logistics. JNPA is a major container-handling and logistics anchor. India's major ports handled about 855 million tonnes of cargo in FY 2024-25.

## Cybersecurity and Critical Infrastructure Environment

India's cybersecurity and critical infrastructure environment is characterized by CERT-In systems, NCIIPC systems, incident-response coordination infrastructure, and critical-infrastructure protection systems. CERT-In carries continuity through national incident-response, alerting, analysis, advisory, and emergency coordination functions. NCIIPC preserves the national critical-infrastructure protection environment.

## Global Digital Public Infrastructure and Cross-Border Integration Environment

India's global digital public infrastructure and cross-border integration environment is characterized by India Stack Global systems, UPI-PayNow linkage systems, cross-border remittance systems, and globally connected trade infrastructure. India Stack Global carries continuity through an outward-facing digital-public-infrastructure export and interoperability framing. The UPI-PayNow linkage and related remittance functions preserve documented international payment-linkage environments.

## Structural Constraints

The current India profile preserves mixed-provider infrastructure dependency structures, limited sovereign compute evidence beyond research-network systems, bounded IX-centrality evidence beyond documented exchange systems, bounded nationwide telecom-market visibility within cited materials, bounded cyber-governance visibility beyond public-sector coordination systems, bounded logistics-topology visibility beyond documented maritime systems, and cross-border and globally integrated infrastructure dependency boundaries.

## Profile Summary Statement

India appears in the profile layer as a large-scale digital-public-infrastructure jurisdiction combining interoperable identity systems, central-bank-operated settlement infrastructure, instant-payment modernization, public-sector cloud continuity, research-network federation, broadband expansion, registry governance, cybersecurity coordination, and globally connected digital-public-infrastructure interfaces.

# India — Signals Layer

Signal derivation constraint: signals derive strictly from evidence.md. This file does not introduce new infrastructure claims, assign routing authority, assign readiness tiers, rank jurisdictions, infer topology placement, or recommend deployment suitability.

## Strategic Position Signals

- Aadhaar identity systems, DigiLocker and UMANG service systems, India Stack interoperability framing, RBI-operated RTGS and NEFT systems, NPCI and UPI payment infrastructure, NIC and MeghRaj public-sector infrastructure, NKN and National Supercomputing Mission systems, NIXI and .IN governance systems, BharatNet and POWERGRID-linked communications systems, CERT-In and NCIIPC coordination systems, major-port throughput systems, and the UPI-PayNow cross-border linkage together signal India as a large-scale digital-public-infrastructure jurisdiction combining interoperable identity systems, central-bank-operated settlement infrastructure, instant-payment modernization, public-sector cloud continuity, research-network federation, broadband expansion, registry governance, cybersecurity coordination, and globally connected digital-public-infrastructure interfaces.

## Digital Governance and Identity Signals

- Aadhaar's role as a verifiable online identity base signals digital-governance continuity supported through interoperable identity systems operating at population scale.
- DigiLocker's role as a secure digital-document storage, sharing, and verification platform signals continuity across document-access and verification functions through state-backed digital-document infrastructure.
- UMANG's function as a unified portal aggregating major citizen-centric services across central and state bodies signals continuity in public-service access through unified service-aggregation systems.
- India Stack Global's framing of Aadhaar, DigiLocker, UMANG, UPI, API Setu, eHospital, eOffice, and eCourt signals nationally coordinated procedural digitization and interoperability across multiple public-service systems.

## Financial Infrastructure and Settlement Signals

- RBI's operation of RTGS signals payment-system continuity supported through central-bank-operated settlement infrastructure with real-time and final settlement characteristics.
- RBI's operation of NEFT as a nation-wide centralised payment system signals continuity across nationwide electronic-transfer systems.
- UPI's documented role in linking multiple bank accounts within a single payment interface signals instant-payment modernization continuity.
- The India-Singapore UPI-PayNow linkage signals continuity in cross-border digital-payment interfaces through an official real-time remittance connection.

## Data Infrastructure and Digital Continuity Signals

- NIC's nationwide ICT role signals public-sector digital continuity supported through nationally coordinated infrastructure spanning NICNET, NKN, National Data Centres, National Cloud, and hosted government systems.
- The distributed National Data Centre footprint across Delhi, Pune, Hyderabad, Bhubaneswar, and state-capital data centres signals geographically distributed government data-centre continuity.
- MeghRaj's role as a government cloud initiative signals continuity through a public cloud-service framework for scalable delivery of hosted governance systems.

## Research Network and Scientific Compute Signals

- NKN's role as a state-of-the-art pan-India network for the knowledge community signals scientific-network federation continuity.
- The National Supercomputing Mission's distributed supercomputing model signals scientific compute continuity through nationally coordinated systems deployed across multiple sites integrated through NKN.

## Internet Exchange and Registry Governance Signals

- NIXI's role in domestic peering coordination signals exchange continuity through nationally organized peering environments.
- The Government of India's delegation of .IN operations to NIXI, together with the .IN Registry's formal administrative role, signals continuity through nationally administered domain-governance systems.
- IRINN's role in IP-address and AS-number allocation signals continuity in numbering-resource administration.

## Telecommunications and Connectivity Signals

- BharatNet's role as a middle-mile network extending connectivity to Gram Panchayats signals telecommunications continuity through nationwide broadband-expansion systems.
- POWERGRID telecom materials documenting pan-India optic-fibre infrastructure signal continuity through state-linked fiber infrastructure.

## Energy and Grid Coordination Signals

- NLDC's documented role as the apex body to ensure integrated operation of the national power system signals energy-grid continuity through nationally coordinated load-dispatch systems.
- GRID-INDIA's documented coordination role including cross-border power-exchange coordination signals a layered operational coordination structure including trans-national exchange functions.

## Logistics and Global Connectivity Signals

- Major-port cargo throughput growth to about 855 million tonnes in FY 2024-25 signals global logistics continuity through high-throughput maritime infrastructure.
- JNPA's 7.3 million TEU handling signals continuity through large-scale port operations and containerized trade interfaces.

## Cybersecurity and Critical Infrastructure Signals

- CERT-In's national role in incident prevention, response, analysis, alerts, emergency measures, and advisories signals cybersecurity continuity through national incident-response coordination systems.
- NCIIPC's designation as the national nodal agency for protection of Critical Information Infrastructure signals continuity in critical-infrastructure protection through a dedicated national institutional environment.

## Global Digital Public Infrastructure and Cross-Border Integration Signals

- India Stack Global's outward-facing framing signals cross-border institutional integration continuity through digital-public-infrastructure export frameworks.
- The India-Singapore UPI-PayNow linkage signals continuity in international payment-linkage systems through a real-time cross-border remittance interface.
- Major-port throughput and container-handling systems signal globally connected trade infrastructure operating alongside outward-facing digital-public-infrastructure initiatives.

## Constraint Boundary Signals

- MeghRaj and national cloud materials signal infrastructure continuity bounded by mixed-provider infrastructure dependencies rather than a wholly sovereign hyperscale stack.
- The evidence does not document a broader sovereign compute estate beyond research-network systems.
- The evidence does not provide full nationwide telecom-market or 5G visibility within cited materials.
- CERT-In and NCIIPC document public-sector cyber coordination clearly, while the evidence does not provide equivalent visibility across all-sector cyber-governance structures.

# India — Trust Dimensions

Trust derivation constraint: trust dimensions derive strictly from evidence.md and signals.md. This file does not introduce new infrastructure claims, assign routing authority, assign readiness tiers, rank jurisdictions, or infer deployment eligibility.

## Institutional Continuity Dimension

The source layers indicate institutional continuity supported through interoperable identity systems, public digital-service infrastructure, central-bank-operated settlement systems, public-sector cloud environments, registry-governance systems, research-network federation, broadband-expansion systems, and cybersecurity coordination structures operating at population scale. Aadhaar, DigiLocker, UMANG, and India Stack indicate continuity across identity, document access, service aggregation, and procedural digitization inside a shared national digital-public-infrastructure environment. RBI, NEFT, RTGS, NPCI, and UPI indicate continuity in payment-system governance through a layered environment combining central-bank settlement systems with interoperable retail-payment modernization. NIC, National Data Centres, and MeghRaj indicate continuity in public-sector digital administration through nationally coordinated ICT infrastructure, distributed hosting environments, and government cloud frameworks. NKN and the National Supercomputing Mission indicate continuity in research-network federation and scientific-compute coordination. NIXI, the .IN Registry, and IRINN indicate continuity in registry, exchange, and numbering governance. BharatNet, POWERGRID telecom systems, CERT-In, and NCIIPC indicate continuity across broadband expansion, state-linked communications systems, cyber coordination, and critical-infrastructure protection functions. India Stack Global, the UPI-PayNow linkage, and major-port logistics materials indicate that this continuity operates inside outward-facing regional and global interfaces rather than within a closed domestic perimeter.

## Digital Governance and Identity Dimension

The source layers indicate digital-governance continuity supported through interoperable identity systems, digital-document infrastructure, unified public-service aggregation systems, and nationally coordinated procedural digitization environments operating at population scale. Aadhaar indicates continuity through a verifiable digital identity base that can function as a primary identifier for government schemes and service delivery. DigiLocker indicates continuity through a secure digital-document infrastructure supporting storage, sharing, and verification. UMANG indicates continuity through a unified service-access layer spanning central and state service environments. India Stack Global and the broader Digital India framing indicate continuity through a coordinated digital-public-infrastructure model linking identity, payments, document systems, and public-service platforms into a shared procedural environment.

## Financial Infrastructure and Settlement Dimension

The source layers indicate payment-system continuity supported through central-bank-operated settlement infrastructure, nationwide electronic-transfer systems, instant-payment interoperability environments, and cross-border digital-payment interfaces. RBI indicates continuity through direct operation of RTGS and NEFT inside a central-bank-governed settlement and transfer environment. RTGS indicates continuity through real-time settlement finality, while NEFT indicates continuity through a nation-wide centralized transfer environment. NPCI and UPI indicate continuity through interoperable instant-payment infrastructure linked to multiple bank accounts. The India-Singapore UPI-PayNow linkage indicates continuity through an official cross-border payment interface attached to the domestic instant-payment environment.

## Data Infrastructure and Digital Continuity Dimension

The source layers indicate public-sector digital continuity supported through nationally coordinated ICT infrastructure, distributed government data-centre environments, public cloud-service frameworks, and hosted governance platforms. NIC indicates continuity through nationwide ICT infrastructure spanning NICNET, NKN, National Data Centres, National Cloud, and hosted government services. The distributed National Data Centre footprint indicates continuity through multiple government hosting locations. MeghRaj indicates continuity through a public cloud-service framework intended to accelerate e-governance delivery. The hosting of e-Office, e-Courts, e-Transport, and related national platforms inside NIC-linked infrastructure indicates continuity across procedural governance platforms.

## Research Network and Scientific Compute Dimension

The source layers indicate scientific-network federation continuity supported through nationally coordinated research-network infrastructure and distributed supercomputing systems integrated through shared academic-network environments. NKN indicates continuity through a pan-India research-network environment. The National Supercomputing Mission indicates continuity through a nationally distributed supercomputing model. The source layers place this continuity within a nationally coordinated scientific-network and compute federation environment rather than a broader sovereign compute estate extending across all sectors.

## Internet Exchange and Registry Governance Dimension

The source layers indicate registry and exchange continuity supported through nationally administered domain-governance systems, domestic peering coordination environments, and numbering-resource administration systems. NIXI indicates continuity through a neutral domestic peering environment designed to retain domestic traffic within India. The .IN Registry indicates continuity through formal administration of India's country-code top-level domain. IRINN indicates continuity through allocation and registration services for IP addresses and AS numbers.

## Telecommunications and Connectivity Dimension

The source layers indicate telecommunications continuity supported through nationwide broadband-expansion systems, institutional networking environments, state-linked fiber infrastructure, and coordinated communications frameworks. BharatNet indicates continuity through a middle-mile broadband-expansion system extending connectivity from blocks to Gram Panchayats. NKN indicates continuity through a parallel institutional networking layer serving the knowledge community across India. POWERGRID telecom materials indicate continuity through state-linked fiber infrastructure built on transmission-line-linked optical systems.

## Energy and Grid Coordination Dimension

The source layers indicate energy-grid continuity supported through nationally coordinated load-dispatch systems, synchronized national-grid management environments, and operational coordination structures including cross-border exchange functions. NLDC indicates continuity through a standing national operational role for integrated management of the national power system. GRID-INDIA indicates continuity through coordination of synchronous grid restoration, Regional Load Despatch Centre linkage, and national planning feedback. The source layers describe energy continuity through coordinated operational structures rather than through broader claims of industrial-energy autonomy.

## Logistics and Trade Continuity Dimension

The source layers indicate global logistics continuity supported through high-throughput maritime infrastructure, port-expansion systems, and nationally coordinated trade-connectivity environments. Major-port throughput growth indicates continuity through sustained high-volume maritime logistics. JNPA's documented container handling indicates continuity through large-scale containerized trade operations. Port-led industrialisation measures indicate continuity through port-expansion and associated trade-connectivity systems. The source layers document maritime and port-centered logistics continuity while keeping broader multimodal claims bounded to the transport and trade-connectivity systems directly described.

## Cybersecurity and Critical Infrastructure Dimension

The source layers indicate cybersecurity continuity supported through national incident-response coordination systems, critical-infrastructure protection environments, cyber-alert dissemination systems, and vulnerability-coordination mechanisms. CERT-In indicates continuity through a standing national incident-prevention, response, analysis, alerting, and advisory function. NCIIPC indicates continuity through a dedicated national institutional environment for protection of Critical Information Infrastructure. NCIIPC's Responsible Vulnerability Disclosure Program indicates continuity through a formal vulnerability-coordination mechanism tied to critical-infrastructure protection.

## Global Digital Public Infrastructure and Cross-Border Integration Dimension

The source layers indicate cross-border institutional integration continuity supported through digital-public-infrastructure export frameworks, international payment-linkage systems, globally connected trade infrastructure, and outward-facing interoperability initiatives. India Stack Global indicates continuity through an outward-facing digital-public-infrastructure framing presenting India's interoperable digital systems as building blocks for wider international engagement. The India-Singapore UPI-PayNow linkage indicates continuity through a real-time international payment-linkage system. Major-port throughput and container systems indicate continuity through globally connected trade infrastructure operating alongside outward-facing digital-public-infrastructure initiatives.

## Constraint Boundary Dimension

The source layers indicate constraint boundaries reflecting a globally integrated infrastructure environment dependent on mixed-provider infrastructure systems, incomplete sovereign-scale compute visibility, constrained exchange-centrality evidence, and documented public-sector coordination perimeters. MeghRaj and related cloud materials indicate meaningful public-sector cloud continuity while the same source layers indicate a mixed-provider environment rather than evidence of a wholly sovereign hyperscale infrastructure stack. NKN and the National Supercomputing Mission indicate meaningful research-network and distributed-compute continuity while the source layers do not document a broader sovereign compute estate beyond those research-network systems. CERT-In and NCIIPC indicate meaningful public-sector cyber coordination while the source layers do not provide equally detailed visibility into all-sector cyber-governance structures.

## Trust Dimensions Summary Statement

India is documented as a large-scale digital-public-infrastructure jurisdiction combining interoperable identity systems, central-bank-operated settlement infrastructure, instant-payment modernization, public-sector cloud continuity, research-network federation, broadband expansion, registry governance, cybersecurity coordination, and globally connected digital-public-infrastructure interfaces. The source layers indicate continuity across digital governance and identity, payment and settlement systems, public-sector ICT and cloud environments, research-network and distributed compute systems, registry and numbering governance, broadband expansion, energy-grid coordination, maritime trade connectivity, cybersecurity coordination, and outward-facing digital-public-infrastructure integration without assigning readiness tiers, routing authority, or deployment eligibility.

# India — Evidence Layer

## Strategic Position

- UIDAI states that Aadhaar is a 12-digit random number issued to residents of India after a verification process, that it is verifiable online in a cost-effective way, and that it may be used as a basis or primary identifier for delivery of government welfare schemes and programmes.
- DigiLocker is a flagship Ministry of Electronics and IT initiative under Digital India and a secure cloud-based platform for storage, sharing, and verification of documents and certificates.
- Digital India states that India Stack Global was launched to showcase the India Stack and its building blocks globally, and that it currently includes key platforms such as Aadhaar, UPI, API Setu, DigiLocker, UMANG, eHospital, eOffice, and eCourt.
- NPCI materials state that UPI powers multiple bank accounts into a single mobile application and merges banking features, fund routing, and merchant payments. RBI states that RTGS is a continuous real-time gross-settlement system and that NEFT is a nation-wide centralised payment system owned and operated by RBI.
- NIC states that it provides nationwide ICT infrastructure and services for government bodies including NICNET, NKN, National Data Centres, and the National Cloud.
- NIXI states that it was established for peering among ISPs so that domestic traffic is routed within the country rather than abroad. The .IN Registry states that it is the official registry for India's top-level domain under NIXI authority.
- CERT-In states that it is the national cyber-security agency under the Information Technology (Amendment) Act 2008. NCIIPC is the national nodal agency for protection of critical information infrastructure.
- NKN states that it is a state-of-the-art pan-India network for the knowledge community. National Supercomputing Mission infrastructure materials state that the mission aims to create a nationally distributed supercomputing infrastructure integrated through NKN.
- PIB states that India and Singapore launched a real-time UPI-PayNow linkage for cross-border remittances. PIB port materials state that India's major ports handled about 855 million tonnes in FY 2024-25.

## Digital Governance and Identity Infrastructure

- UIDAI states that Aadhaar number is a 12-digit random number issued to residents of India after a defined verification process, that uniqueness is achieved through demographic and biometric de-duplication, and that it is verifiable online in a cost-effective way.
- DigiLocker is a secure cloud-based platform for storage, sharing, and verification of documents and certificates under Digital India.
- UMANG states that it is a unified portal aggregating major citizen-centric services of central and state governments, local bodies, and statutory bodies through mobile apps and the web.
- Digital India states that India Stack Global currently includes 15 key projects and platforms, including Aadhaar, UPI, API Setu, DigiLocker, UMANG, eHospital, eOffice, and eCourt, and frames India's experience as implementation of digital transformation projects at population scale.

Sources:
- UIDAI: https://uidai.gov.in/en/my-aadhaar/about-your-aadhaar.html
- Digital India, India Stack Global: https://www.digitalindia.gov.in/initiative/india-stack-global/
- Digital India, UMANG: https://www.digitalindia.gov.in/initiative/umang/

## Financial Infrastructure and Settlement Systems

- RBI states that RTGS is available on a 24x7x365 basis and that settlement occurs in the books of RBI and is final and irrevocable.
- RBI states that NEFT is a nation-wide centralised payment system owned and operated by RBI, available round the clock throughout the year.
- NPCI materials state that UPI is an instant payment system developed by NPCI, an RBI-regulated entity, that allows instant transfer of money between bank accounts.
- PIB states that India and Singapore launched the real-time linkage between India's UPI and Singapore's PayNow, describing it as a cross-border P2P payment facility intended to make remittances easy, cost-effective, and real time.

Sources:
- RBI RTGS: https://www.rbi.org.in/commonman/english/scripts/faqs.aspx?id=275
- RBI NEFT: https://www.rbi.org.in/commonman/English/Scripts/FAQs.aspx?Id=274
- NPCI UPI: https://www.npci.org.in/what-we-do/upi/product-overview
- PIB UPI-PayNow: https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1900976

## Data Infrastructure and Digital Continuity

- NIC states that National Data Centres have been established at Delhi, Pune, Hyderabad, and Bhubaneswar, together with 37 small data centres at state capitals, and that these form the core of e-governance infrastructure in India.
- NIC states that MeghRaj, the Government of India's cloud initiative, is intended to accelerate delivery of e-services and offers multiple service models including PaaS, IaaS, SaaS, container services, and AI services.
- PIB states that a national cloud infrastructure has been established under Digital India and that cloud services from multiple empanelled providers are part of the government cloud environment.

Sources:
- NIC Services: https://www.nic.gov.in/services/
- NIC Data Centre: https://www.nic.gov.in/service/data-centre/
- NIC National Cloud: https://www.nic.gov.in/service/national-cloud/

## Research Network and Compute Infrastructure

- NKN states that it is a state-of-the-art pan-India network for the knowledge community.
- National Supercomputing Mission infrastructure materials state that the mission aims to achieve self-reliance in supercomputing and envisions a national infrastructure of supercomputing systems distributed across the country and seamlessly integrated through the National Knowledge Network.

Sources:
- National Knowledge Network: https://nkn.gov.in/
- National Supercomputing Mission: https://nsmindia.in/infrastructure/

## Internet Exchange and Registry Infrastructure

- NIXI states that it is a not-for-profit organisation established for peering among ISPs so that domestic traffic can be routed within India instead of being carried abroad.
- NIXI states that the Government of India delegated operation of the .IN Registry to NIXI in 2004, and that IRINN provides allocation and registration services for IP addresses and AS numbers in India.
- The .IN Registry states that it is the official .IN registry appointed by the Government of India and operated under the authority of NIXI.

Sources:
- NIXI About Us: https://nixi.in/nc-about-us/
- .IN Registry: https://www.registry.in/about-registry

## Telecommunications and Digital Infrastructure

- BBNL materials state that BharatNet is a middle-mile network from blocks to Gram Panchayats and that the BharatNet/NOFN programme was intended to cover around 250,000 Gram Panchayats across roughly 6,600 blocks and 641 districts.
- POWERGRID materials state that the company leveraged its pan-India transmission network through optical ground wire and that its telecom subsidiary operates a pan-India overhead optic-fibre network.

Sources:
- BBNL BharatNet: https://bbnl.nic.in/index1.aspx?lsid=536&lev=1&lid=445&langid=1
- POWERGRID telecom: https://www.powergrid.in/en/telecom

## Energy and Grid Coordination Infrastructure

- POSOCO materials state that the National Load Despatch Centre was constituted under Ministry of Power notification and is the apex body to ensure integrated operation of the national power system.
- GRID-INDIA materials state that its functions include coordination for restoration of synchronous national-grid operation with Regional Load Despatch Centres and coordination for trans-national exchange of power.

Sources:
- POSOCO NLDC: https://posoco.in/about-us/functions-of-nldc/
- GRID-INDIA: https://grid-india.in/en/about-us/mission-objectives-functions/

## Logistics and Global Connectivity Infrastructure

- PIB states that India's major ports handled about 855 million tonnes of cargo in FY 2024-25, up from 819 million tonnes in FY 2023-24.
- PIB states that container throughput rose by 10 percent and that Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority handled 7.3 million TEUs in FY 2024-25.

Sources:
- PIB Major Ports FY 2024-25: https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2128329

## Cybersecurity and Critical Infrastructure Protection

- CERT-In states that it is a functional organisation of MeitY with the objective of securing Indian cyberspace and that under the Information Technology (Amendment) Act 2008 it serves as the national agency for collection, analysis, and dissemination of cyber-incident information.
- NCIIPC was created under Section 70A of the Information Technology Act and serves as the national nodal agency for protection of Critical Information Infrastructure. NCIIPC runs a Responsible Vulnerability Disclosure Program for vulnerabilities affecting Critical Information Infrastructures.

Sources:
- CERT-In: https://www.cert-in.org.in/s2cMainServlet?pageid=CHARTMISSION
- NCIIPC: https://nciipc.gov.in/index.html

## Global Digital Public Infrastructure and Cross-Border Integration

- Digital India states that India Stack Global was launched to showcase India Stack globally and that lessons from India Stack are available for the world to adopt. The portal currently includes 15 key projects and platforms presented in all UN languages.
- PIB states that the India-Singapore UPI-PayNow linkage created a real-time cross-border payment facility and identified Singapore as the first country with which such a cross-border P2P payment facility was launched.
- RBI states that NEFT is available for one-way funds transfers from India to Nepal.
- PIB port materials document India's major ports as high-throughput international trade interfaces.

Sources:
- Digital India India Stack Global: https://www.digitalindia.gov.in/initiative/india-stack-global/
- PIB UPI-PayNow: https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1900976

# India — Change Log

## Initial Package Creation

The India jurisdiction package was created as part of Atlas global jurisdiction normalization.

The package includes: evidence.md, signals.md, trust-dimensions.md, metadata.md, profile.md, builder-mode.md, and change-log.md.

## Evidence Layer Construction

evidence.md established Aadhaar identity systems, DigiLocker systems, UMANG systems, India Stack interoperability systems, Digital India infrastructure, Reserve Bank of India systems, RTGS infrastructure, NEFT systems, UPI infrastructure, NPCI systems, MeghRaj government cloud systems, NIC infrastructure, National Data Centres, NKN systems, National Supercomputing Mission systems, NIXI systems, .IN Registry systems, IRINN systems, BharatNet systems, NOFN systems, POWERGRID telecom infrastructure, NLDC systems, GRID-INDIA systems, major-port throughput systems, JNPA logistics systems, CERT-In systems, NCIIPC systems, India Stack Global systems, UPI-PayNow linkage systems, and cross-border remittance systems.

## Metadata Classification

metadata.md classified India as a large-scale digital-public-infrastructure jurisdiction, a national digital identity and interoperability environment, a central-bank payment modernization and settlement-governance environment, a public-sector cloud and procedural-digitization environment, a registry and numbering-governance environment, a research-network and distributed-compute federation environment, a telecommunications and broadband-expansion environment, an energy-grid operational-coordination environment, a cybersecurity and critical-infrastructure coordination environment, a trade and maritime-connectivity environment, and a globally integrated digital-public-infrastructure participation environment.

## Structural Constraints Recorded

Normalization preserved mixed-provider infrastructure dependency structures, absence of wholly sovereign hyperscale infrastructure evidence, limited sovereign compute evidence beyond research-network systems, bounded IX-centrality evidence beyond documented exchange systems, bounded nationwide telecom-market visibility within cited materials, bounded cyber-governance visibility beyond public-sector coordination systems, bounded logistics-topology visibility beyond documented maritime systems, and cross-border and globally integrated infrastructure dependency boundaries.

## Package Completion Status

Normalization status: complete
